newsitem.title: UK: Lower European sugar output could cut stocks-Licht.
newsitem.headline: Lower European sugar output could cut stocks-Licht.

text.p: The changes in Europe's expected sugar output in 1997/98 should have little effect on world prices but could contribute to a limited reduction in global stocks, F.O. Licht said on Thursday.
"The changes in European output and possible reduction compared with 1996/97 are unlikely to have much impact on world market prices," Licht said in a report.
"However, taken in combination with likely falls in output in other parts of the world, a limited reduction in world stocks may be possible."
Licht said stocks could fall by more than 1.5 million tonnes over the 1997/98 season but did not give any estimate of actual stock levels.
Earlier, it estimated sugar output in western Europe at 21.23 million tonnes raw value for 1997/98 (September/August), up from 20.67 million tonnes the previous season.
But the increase in the western nations was expected to be offset by declines in the eastern half, especially after floods devastated farmland in Poland.
Licht forecast sugar output in eastern Europe at 8.68 million tonnes, compared with a previous 9.67 million.
All major producers in the region were expected to show a decline, the sharpest in Poland where output would fall by 540,000 tonnes to 1.96 million tonnes.
